items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I played the Savoy Ballroom with Lucky Millinder

ctx.x: Yeah. Did you have occasion to play the Savoy?

The Savoy Ballroom, oh yeah, I played the Savoy Ballroom with Lucky Millinder, I played in there with Jimmy Lunceford’s band, I subbed in there a few times with Erskine Hawkins band, Jimmy Rushing had a band, I played with them a few times, I played a lot at the Savoy Ballroom. That was quite a place.
I just wish I could have been there. It sounds like a great scene.

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I used to be – when I was in the band for a time, I was the straw boss. I used to rehearse the band for him.

ctx.x: Lucky’s band was nice. He had an interesting band too. Lucky was a very innovative bandleader. He would try anything, anything that was different. His band was different than any of the other bands I had played with, again, not as daring as Lionel Hampton, but he would attempt things that other guys, other bands just seemed not to bother with. He also was very adept at hiring good players. He didn’t mind spending a little extra money to get a better player, if he thought he could.

I used to be – when I was in the band for a time, I was the straw boss. I used to rehearse the band for him. He didn’t read music, incidentally. He had tremendous ears, but he wasn’t a musician – Lucky wasn’t.
How did he get into all that?
